newsitem.title: POLAND: Britain's Fergie happy in single life with Andrew.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Fergie happy in single life with Andrew.

text.p: Britain's Duchess of York said on Monday she and her ex-husband Prince Andrew are happy leading single lives under the same roof in what was once their marital home.
She told a news conference in Warsaw: "It may be very extraordinary to most people but we manage to retain our independent single lives while living under the same roof."
The Duchess, known by the nickname Fergie, returned to the family home, Sunninghill Park House, last February.

"We are happy with that and the children are happy with that. It is good harmony and it shows in the children," said the Duchess, who with daughters Beatrice,8, and Eugenie, 7, has been staying at the home the couple built after their 1986 wedding.
"We both believe in joint parenting and we both believe in the fact that we can put aside all our worries...so that we can be good parents for our two children," she added.

Asked to comment on British tabloid reports that Prince Andrew had allegedly lost patience and wanted the Duchess out of the house after learning that she was going out on dates, she retorted: "We are in 1997 -- three years off the millenium."

The Duchess, who was divorced a year ago from Queen Elizabeth's second son Andrew, was in Poland visiting and raising funds for Children in Crisis, a charity she founded which runs a mountain resort and haven for sick children mostly from Poland's heavily-polluted southern industrial regions.
